intro: An edge detector combines nearby pixels. Trace the local multiply-and-sum operation before introducing a convolution library.
task: Return valid two-dimensional cross-correlation of an image with a supplied kernel, at stride one and with no padding.
requirements: image and kernel are nonempty finite two-dimensional arrays. The kernel must fit within the image on both axes.
Multiply each image window by the kernel as supplied; do not flip the kernel.
Return a NumPy array with shape (image_height - kernel_height + 1, image_width - kernel_width + 1).
Do not modify inputs. Raise ValueError for the invalid shapes, ranges, or non-finite numeric inputs described above. Numerical checks use moderate finite values unless stated otherwise.

hints.title: Choose the representation
hints.body: Allocate the smaller output first, then visit each valid top-left window position.

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: Use an asymmetric kernel to check that you have not accidentally flipped it.

explanation: A local filter shares the same weights across positions. Cross-correlation takes a weighted sum of each local image window, making the operation sensitive to spatial patterns.
The kernel stays in its supplied orientation. Many neural-network convolution layers use this cross-correlation convention; mathematical convolution would reverse the kernel.
Try the kernel [1, -1] on a constant row and on a step. Explain why the response is zero in flat regions and changes sign when you reverse the edge.
